draft.title: Expected value and variance
card: The expected value is the long-run mean of X. E(X) = sum of x × Pr(X = x), taken over every value of x.
The variance is Var(X) = E(X²) − (E(X))². Find E(X²) by adding x² × Pr(X = x). The standard deviation is the square root of Var(X).
Example: X takes 0, 1, 2 with probabilities 0.5, 0.3, 0.2. E(X) = 0 + 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.7.
draft.remember: Find E(X), then E(X²), then subtract the square of E(X). Take the square root for the standard deviation.

a.q: X takes the values 1, 2, 3 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3. What is E(X)?
a.why: E(X) = 1 × 0.2 + 2 × 0.5 + 3 × 0.3 = 0.2 + 1 + 0.9 = 2.1. Averaging the values 1, 2, 3 gives 2, which ignores the probabilities.
a.clue: Multiply each value by its own probability, then add.

b.q: A game gives a score X of 0, 2 or 4 with probabilities 0.4, 0.4, 0.2. What is Var(X)?
b.clue: Subtract the square of the mean from E(X²).

b.q: A game gives a score X of 0, 2 or 4 with probabilities 0.4, 0.4, 0.2. What is Var(X)?
b.why: E(X) = 0 + 0.8 + 0.8 = 1.6 and E(X²) = 0 + 1.6 + 3.2 = 4.8, so Var(X) = 4.8 − 1.6² = 4.8 − 2.56 = 2.24. The tempting 2.56 is only (E(X))², and 3.2 comes from subtracting 1.6 without squaring it.
b.clue: Subtract the square of the mean from E(X²).
